title: Abstention & Routing Harness
summary: How can a routing system abstain reliably on mixed, malformed, conflicting or out-of-domain requests without mistaking model confidence for authority?
evidence_level: Measured rule baselines and adversarial robustness on synthetic cases; no model results
contribution: Concept, research direction, evaluation design and editorial: ilghar.studio.
architecture: Recorded or mocked model proposal adapter

results.caveat: test probes written by rule author; not blind

limitations: All items are synthetic; no model was run. Mock results are labelled as mocks.
Test probes were written by the same author after the rule existed, so they are not blind.
Historical multilingual-reader fixtures are summaries, not re-runs, and measure a different task.
Reviews so far are self-reviews; no independent reviewer yet.
Illustrations are editorial images only; the native diagram is authoritative.
pitch: A small, strict referee that decides which review desk an incoming item belongs to, and knows when to say “I don’t know, a person should look at this.”
problem: Picture an archive of mixed material: spreadsheets, chat threads, notes in English and German. Every item has to reach the right review desk. A language model can suggest a desk instantly, and it sounds just as sure when it is wrong.

The original study behind this project made that concrete. A local multilingual reader proposed queues on a twenty-item historical fixture and failed 12 of 20 (by my notes from that study, not re-run here), including one “false winner”: it confidently picked a desk for an item that belonged to neither. Confidence was being mistaken for authority.

This harness turns the lesson into rules you can test. A suggestion is only accepted when the item’s type was confirmed independently, the text is readable and harmless, the budget is valid, and every reader agrees. Everything else goes to a person, with a reason written in plain language. The harness never moves a document; it only advises.

audience.who: People building triage or routing on top of language models
audience.why: A ready-made set of gates, reason codes and metrics for measuring how often the system admits work it should have refused.
Every decision carries a reason code and a stable identity hash, so runs can be compared and audited line by line.
A prioritised human review queue that explains why each item was held back, instead of a silent “unknown”.

how.title: Record + independent scope label
how.body: Each case carries its text and a scope label confirmed by someone other than the model (for example, “this really is a spreadsheet”). Without it, nothing is admitted.

how.title: Validation gates
how.body: Invisible or empty text, requests to change permissions or take actions, and invalid or exhausted budgets are stopped before any proposal is read.

how.title: Recorded proposals
how.body: Proposals from one or more readers arrive as JSON (recorded, mocked or from the local keyword rule). No network call and no model loading happen inside the harness.

how.title: Abstain or advise
how.body: Malformed, missing, self-abstaining or conflicting proposals are held back. Only clean agreement becomes an advisory route; documents are never moved.

how.title: Metrics with denominators
how.body: Coverage, selective accuracy, false acceptance and per-class confusion, always as counts over a stated n with Wilson intervals, never a bare percentage.

how.title: Human review queue
how.body: Every held-back item becomes a row in a prioritised worklist with the reason in plain words.

commands.what: Apply the policy to 16 hand-written cases with mock proposals. Writes decisions.json and report.json. Mock data, not a model result.

End-to-end slice: 20 cleared EN/DE queue items plus 7 out-of-domain and mixed probes, through the local keyword proposer and the policy. The rule was tuned on this same fixture, so this is not held-out.
Validate the versioned case collection against schemas/case.schema.json and write a hashed manifest.
Compare three baselines on dev and test: always abstain, always pick the majority desk, and the keyword rule. Values are [coverage, selective accuracy, false acceptance].
Run the 34-case adversarial suite (invisible text, surrogates, NaN budgets, oversized proposals) and classify held-out errors.
Turn decisions into a prioritised human worklist (Markdown + JSON) with a plain-language reason for every held-back item.

commands.what: Score cases with the cost/risk policy (expected cost of each route vs the cost of handing to a person), sweep the support threshold, and write a confusion report (expected vs decided: spreadsheet / conversation / person) as JSON and reports/…/index.html. MOCK: the confidences in this fixture are hand-written to demonstrate the mechanism; the numbers are not a result, and the calibration is in-sample.

schemas.what: One case: id, text, scope_verified, case_class, expected_route, requests_used (budget), proposals, fixture_kind, known_limitation.
One decision: route, abstained, reason_code, identity hash, advisory_only, can_move_documents=false.
Run report: fixture hash, rubric, run kind (mock, rule, recorded) and metrics with denominators.
